title: elephant-1 decide
description: Baseten’s System One decision prompt on a text or JSON state, optionally with pictures and videos: every question answered from one shared-prefix prefill.

state.description: Text or any JSON value, rendered in the key order sent; null for none. Pictures and videos sent in media are placed where the state says <image:1>, <video:2>, … (each once, in order), e.g. {"screen": "<image:1>"}. Over MCP an object loses its key order; to keep it, also send ordered_json: {"state": "<the same state as JSON text>"}.

questions.description: Question name → question. Names come back as the answers' keys; they are not shown to the model. Their order and each choice's option order set the prompt; over MCP send questions as their JSON text to keep both.

media.description: Pictures and videos the state refers to by <image:N> / <video:N> (N from 1, each once, in order, of the item's own kind), as the makers' media list. A video is a list of pre-extracted frames with an fps. Resized as the model's processors do: a picture at most 16,384 tokens; a video at most 768 tokens per pair of frames, up to 960 for a 5-frame list, where the processor's rounding allows 1.25 times its per-frame cap.

path.description: Existing absolute local image path inside Arsenal's inbox or jobs folder (upload it first).

frames.description: The video's stills in order, all one size (PNG or JPEG), each {"path": absolute local path}. Pairs of frames share one time step, so an odd count repeats the last frame.

path.description: Existing absolute local image path inside Arsenal's inbox or jobs folder (upload it first).

fps.description: Frames per second of the list, which sets the timestamps the model sees; default 1.0.

model.description: elephant-1; omit on this model’s operation endpoint.

bits.description: Required precision; 0 accepts the loaded FP16 and 16 matches it. Any other value returns 409.

merge.description: The shared state prefix is always used.

question.description: A typed question about the state. Unknown fields are ignored.

type.description: noul = yes/no (answer P(yes)); choice = one of named options; score = an ordered level.

instructions.description: The question, as text or structured JSON. Optional; null or absent uses the default wording.

criteria.description: noul: optional {"true", "false"}; choice: options; score: levels, lowest first.

true.description: What this side means: text or structured JSON; null or absent uses the default wording.

false.description: What this side means: text or structured JSON; null or absent uses the default wording.

criteria.description: Optional {"true", "false"} descriptions; other keys are ignored, as the makers’ schema does.
Option label → description (null for the bare label). Labels are compared as exact strings.

items.description: What the option means: text, structured JSON, or null for the bare option.

criteria.description: Level descriptions, lowest first; levels are answered as "0", "1", …
